description:
TARGET A, MEASURED s473x (2026-09-19) while profiling `ovlsub` for the first
time.  PRE-EXISTING; not built in round 34 because it is not one lever.

WHAT THE PROFILE SAYS.  sb-sprof :cpu over the `ovlsub` row (N=3 M, 3 085 and
3 196 samples in two agreeing runs, scratch/s473x/prof.pl in the s473x
worktree).  The row's loop is

    my $y = $x - 3; $s += "$y";

on a class with `-` and `""` overloads whose `new` is `bless { v => ... }`.
The brief asked whether the 3.4x is the overload lookup, the fallback path, the
string conversion or boxing.  It is the last two, and the answer to the first
is that the lookup is ALREADY CHEAP:

    p-find-overload        8.4 % TOTAL, 0.6 % SELF   (#582's own-class cache)
    p-call-overload        3.7 % total, 0.7 % self
    %p---slow              5.5 % total, 0.8 % self

The two big groups are:

  (a) THE STRING -> NUMBER COERCION, 23.5 % â `$s += "$y"`.  CLOSED in round 34
      by %p-plain-integer-string (ovlsub +29.5 %, 3.4x perl -> 2.6x).

  (b) THE PER-OBJECT HASH TABLE, ~20 % â this task.  Every iteration builds a
      fresh CL hash table for a ONE-KEY object:

        p-hash                          12.7 % total, 1.8 self
        p-bless                          5.4 % total, 1.1 self
        gethash/equal                   10.0 % total, 4.7 self
        puthash/equal                    7.5 % total, 2.0 self
        (insert-at :in TARGET-HASH-TABLE) 5.1 % total
        sxhash-recurse 4.3 + perhaps-truncated-equal-hash 3.9
          + %sxhash-string/truncating 1.3
        grow-hash-table 3.8, %make-hash-table 3.5,
        make-hash-table-using-defaults 1.0, %alloc-hash-table 1.3,
        pick-table-methods 0.7, equal-not-inline 0.8

      (The groups overlap: p-hash's TOTAL contains the hash-table calls it
      makes.  De-overlapped it is ~20 % of the row.)

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE LEVER.  A Perl object is an `EQUAL` hash table with
string keys, and that is the representation `docs/ir-spec.md` Â§2 fixes: `%$obj`,
`keys`, `delete`, `exists`, a tied class, `Data::Dumper` and every module that
walks an object's fields all read it.  The candidates, none of them sized here:
  * a SMALL-TABLE representation (an alist or a pair vector below N keys) with
    promotion on growth â the cost is that every hash accessor grows an arm,
    and `%p-hash-elem-cell`'s promotion-in-place has to work on it;
  * pre-sizing the table from the constructor's key count (`p-hash` already
    knows the literal's length) â cheap, narrow, and the only part that could
    be tried on its own;
  * interning the key strings so `sxhash` is not recomputed per store â the
    hash of a CONSTANT key is recomputable at emission time, but the table is
    EQUAL and SBCL owns the hashing.

MEASURE FIRST, and the row is ready: `perl tools/bench-exec.pl ovlsub` plus
`methret` as the object control.  A lever must clear 20 % of the row on its own
(the round-33/34 bar), and `ovlsub` has a 6-11 % run-to-run spread of its own,
so it must be A/B'd with a control pair in the same window (BENCH_RT_B), never
board to board.
subject: TARGET A, MEASURED s473x: the per-object HASH TABLE is ~20 % of the `ovlsub` row -- a fresh EQUAL table with string keys per `bless {v=>...}`, and the overload lookup it was blamed on is 0.6 % self (#582 already took it)
